title: The Moral Machine Experiment on Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Presenting LLMs with text-based autonomous driving moral dilemmas (Moral Machine scenarios) and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE) to measure the preference for saving humans versus pets.

Using randomized Moral Machine scenarios to compute the AMCE and evaluate the model's preference for saving individuals with perceived higher social value (e.g., executives) versus those with lower social value (e.g., criminals).
Evaluating LLM choices in binary moral dilemmas to calculate the AMCE of saving female versus male characters.
Analyzing model responses in Moral Machine scenarios to compute the AMCE of prioritizing younger characters over older characters.
Using constrained randomization in moral dilemmas to calculate the AMCE of choosing to save physically fit individuals (e.g., athletes) versus less fit or obese individuals.
Presenting scenarios where pedestrians are either crossing legally or illegally to calculate the AMCE of saving law-abiding individuals versus those flouting the law.
